blocks.text: Verified 55+ manufactured-home parks and co-ops: what the sources show

These are the 55+ places named in public sources where you can own the home. Pad rent, shares and fees quoted below are listing-stated for one home on one date, not a park tariff, so confirm them with the park. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Cedar Creek Estates — 3031 200 St (Brookswood, Township of Langley)

Manufactured-home park; listings record "Age Restricted 55+," adult-oriented community features, pets allowed with restrictions, rentals not allowed, leasehold (non-strata) tenure and a community centre in the park. Pad rent for this park: Not confirmed — no park-operator source stating a current pad rent was obtained; any figure in a listing is listing-stated for that home at that date.
Fernridge Park — 20071 24 Ave (Brookswood, Township of Langley)

Manufactured-home park; listings describe a "55-plus" park with no pets and no rentals, park manager approval required, and a clubhouse. Pad rent for this park: Not confirmed — no park-operator source stating a current pad rent was obtained.
Pineridge — 2270 196 St (Brookswood, Township of Langley)

Manufactured-home park; a current listing calls it "one of Brookswood's most beloved 55+ mobile home communities" and records "Restricted Age: 55+," leasehold non-strata tenure. Pad rent for this park: Not confirmed — no park-operator source stating a current pad rent was obtained.
Rules that affect 55+ park homes

items.t: The governing law for a rented pad is provincial, not municipal: Manufactured home site tenancies are governed by BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act (MHPTA) wherever the park sits; in that tenure the tenant owns the manufactured home and rents the site under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, and landlords and tenants must have a written tenancy agreement for the site.

The 2026 pad-rent increase limit: 2.3% plus a proportional amount: For manufactured home site tenancies the 2026 limit is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees; the 2027 limit is 2.2% plus the proportional amount. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of manufactured home sites in the park.

How an increase may be given: only with 3 full months' written notice, only once every 12 months, and only up to the yearly limit; the landlord may not round up and may not carry forward an unused portion of a prior year's limit, and if proper notice was not given the increase takes effect on the earliest date that would comply.

Above-limit increases need an order, not a notice: A landlord may apply to the Residential Tenancy Branch (RTB Form 52) for an additional increase for financial loss from increased operating or financing costs, or for substantial and essential repairs or renovations that are reasonable, necessary and not expected to recur. Tenants do not have to pay an increase above the legal amount and may deduct an overpayment from future rent or apply for dispute resolution.

Buying a park home does not reset the pad rent (MHPTA s. 28 assignment): Assignment permanently transfers the site tenancy to the buyer; a tenant may assign only with the landlord's prior written consent (or consent deemed given under the regulations), an order of the director, or where the tenancy agreement authorizes it; before asking, the seller must give the proposed buyer written copies of the park rules and the relevant parts of the tenancy agreement; the landlord cannot charge a fee for consent; and on assignment the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same, as does the scheduled date of a subsequent rent increase.

A park's 55+ rule is a park rule, not a strata bylaw: The Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Regulation (B.C. Reg. 481/2003) expressly recognises a park where every site is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 (per Human Rights Code s. 10(2)(b)(i)) and allows a park landlord to refuse an assignment where the proposed purchaser does not meet the park's age requirement. The Strata Property Act exemptions below do not answer a park occupancy question — get the park's rules in writing.

Park closure / conversion (MHPTA s. 42): where a landlord intends to convert all or a significant part of a park to another use, the landlord must have all necessary government permits and approvals in place before issuing notice, must give 12 months' notice, and must pay the tenant $20,000 compensation on or before the notice's effective date; the tenant may move out early on at least 10 days' written notice, may dispute within 15 days, may in defined circumstances apply for additional compensation of the home's assessed value minus the $20,000, and if the landlord does not take steps toward the stated conversion within a reasonable period the landlord must pay the greater of $5,000 or 12 months' rent.

Registration and the CSA label gate every park purchase: In BC the sale, transfer or purchase of a manufactured home is only effective if registered with the Manufactured Home Registry, through a lawyer or notary filing the original signed and witnessed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership forms; a home may not be sold without its original legible CSA decal (Z-240 for mobile homes, A-277 for modular), and a lost label requires Technical Safety BC re-certification. A permit to move a home is issued by the Registry, a tax certificate for transport purposes is required (with exceptions including a move to a different pad within the same park), and the transport permit expires 30 days after issue.

Tax on a park home excludes the land: The Province states a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value will not include the value of the land if the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.
What pad rent includes is park-by-park: Not confirmed as a general Langley statement

For comparison — the strata rules that apply to Langley's strata 55+ complexes, not its parks: under the Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2, only a 55+ age bylaw is valid since Nov 24, 2022 (Bill 44); the bylaw restricts residency, not ownership; Strata Property Regulation 7.01 exempts legacy residents, live-in caregivers, and since May 1, 2023 also a younger spouse/partner, children under 19 in the specified resident's care, and adult children cared for before 19; and strata rental-restriction bylaws are void province-wide since Nov 24, 2022, while short-term rental bylaws remain allowed. None of that governs a pad tenancy.

Two zoning bylaws, kept separate: Langley City complexes and any City park sit under Langley City Zoning Bylaw 2025 No. 3300 (City SSMUH Bylaw 3284, adopted June 17, 2024; City suite cap is the lesser of 100 m² and 40%); Township parks — including all three verified Brookswood parks and Pioneer Park — sit under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (Township SSMUH Bylaw 6020, adopted November 18, 2024: 3 units on lots ≤280 m², 4 on lots to <4,050 m², larger lots ineligible, no 6-unit tier; Township suite cap 120 m²).

blocks.text: Good to know before you buy a park home

items.t: There is no Langley pad-rent average to look up — and a page that prints one has not sourced it. Neither the Province, the Township, the City nor SnapStats publishes a park-level or average pad rent for Langley; SnapStats publishes no manufactured-home category and no rent figure of any kind. The only official "number" in this topic is the increase formula.

The proportional amount makes two parks' increases differ in the same year. It is the park's own levy plus regulated-utility change divided by that park's own site count — so the same 2.3% headline limit for 2026 produces a different dollar increase at Cedar Creek Estates than at Fernridge Park or Pineridge. Ask the specific park for its last proportional-amount calculation.
All of Langley's verified 55+ pad-rental parks are in one Township pocket. A buyer fixed on a 55+ park in Langley is, in practice, shopping Brookswood — or the Aldergrove co-op.

A transfer does not trigger a market re-pricing of the pad. Unlike a strata purchase, where fees are whatever the current budget says, an MHPTA assignment carries the existing pad rent and the existing next-increase date to the new tenant — the seller's rent history is part of what a buyer is acquiring, and it is documented in the tenancy agreement the seller must share before consent is sought.

The CSA label is a hard gate, not a detail. A manufactured home without its original legible CSA decal (Z-240 mobile, A-277 modular) cannot be sold until Technical Safety BC re-certification — label status is a price and timeline fact on every Langley park purchase, and it is the dividing line between renovated, readily saleable park homes and original-condition fixer product.

"55+" in a Langley park and "55+" in a Langley strata are different legal objects. The park rule sits in tenancy regulation and park rules and can support refusing an assignment; the strata rule sits in a registered bylaw under ss. 123.1/123.2 with Regulation 7.01 exemptions. A couple who qualify to live in a Parkway Estates strata unit on a spousal exemption have no automatic equivalent right in a Brookswood park.

Township taxes have two penalty steps that park owners still pay on the home. Township of Langley property taxes and utility fees were due Thursday, July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to current-year taxes unpaid at midnight July 2, 2026, with a further 5% at midnight September 3, 2026, and utility fees are billed separately. All three verified 55+ parks are in the Township, so this calendar — not Langley City's — is the one their owners follow.

items.t: "Langley" here spans two municipalities with separate bylaws — the Township of Langley and the City of Langley. Pad tenancy law itself is provincial, not municipal: manufactured home site tenancies are governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act wherever the park sits.

Tenure definition the whole page turns on: in a manufactured home park, many tenants own their manufactured home and rent the site it sits on, under a Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement; where both the home and the site are rented, a Residential Tenancy Agreement applies instead.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: streets and boundaries

items.t: Langley is two municipalities: the Township of Langley and the City of Langley. Pad tenancy law is provincial, but park zoning, permits and redevelopment approvals sit with the municipality the park is in.

In the Township, Cedar Creek Estates Manufactured Home Park at 3031 200 Street, at the northwest corner of 200 Street and 30 Avenue in Brookswood, was redesignated Manufactured Home Park by Bylaw No. 5320, and the Township's 2023 Booth, Fernridge and Rinn report states there are four other manufactured home parks in the Fernridge Neighbourhood Plan area.
The Township's Booth Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw No. 6008, adopted June 10, 2024) maps a Manufactured Home Park designation to the MH-1 Residential Manufactured Home Park Zone.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: the housing stock

items.t: Tenure first: a home on a rented pad is not land ownership. The buyer owns the home as a chattel and rents the pad (the manufactured home site) from the park landlord under a written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement, governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act (MHPTA).
Ask for the agreement, not a verbal list of inclusions.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Disputes go to the Residential Tenancy Branch (RTB) by dispute resolution: a tenant who is charged above the legal limit does not have to pay the excess, can deduct an overpayment from future rent with a written explanation, or can apply for dispute resolution for an order that the landlord comply.

Township permit layer: placing a home in a Township park needs a building permit, the Park Manager's acceptance and signature on the building plans, and compliance with the Township's Mobile Home Park Bylaw, Building Bylaw and, in some parks, development permits.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Two different RTB forms do two different jobs: the Notice of Standard Rent Increase, Manufactured Home Site (Form RTB-11a), covers the standard increase, and a landlord seeking an increase above the limit applies on the Application for Additional Rental Increase Form (RTB Form 52), which cannot be filed online.
A landlord cannot round up the increase, cannot carry forward an unused part of a past year's limit, and an increase given on short notice simply takes effect on the earliest date that would comply.

Dispute deadlines are short and different: 5 days for a 10-day notice for non-payment, 10 days for a one-month notice, and 15 days for a 12-month park-conversion notice, each counted from receiving the notice.
If the landlord does not take steps toward the stated conversion within a reasonable period after a 12-month notice, the landlord must pay the greater of $5,000 or 12 months' rent.

A Township home must meet CSA (Canadian Standards Association) A277 or CAN/CSA Z240 MH Series standards, and in older parks a setback that cannot be met can require a Board of Variance application before a permit issues.
The sale itself is only effective once registered with the Manufactured Home Registry, through a lawyer or notary filing the signed Bill of Sale and Notice to Transfer or Change Ownership forms.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: costs and taxes

items.t: Property tax on the home: the Province states a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value does not include the value of the land where the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.
Municipal rates for context, 2026: the City of Langley's total residential rate is 4.2067 per $1,000 of taxable value on its 2026 Property Tax Rates sheet.

Speculation and Vacancy Tax: both the City of Langley and the Township of Langley are on the Province's list of taxable areas in the Metro Vancouver Regional District, as is the City of Maple Ridge; whether the tax applies to a specific park home depends on the owner's declaration and exemptions, not on the pad.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: getting around

items.t: Langley Centre is the bus exchange for both Langleys, and TransLink's regional connections map shows it as a bus node with route 595 running from it across the Golden Ears Bridge to Maple Meadows Station.

Highway access is Fraser Highway (Highway 1A) through both Langleys and Highway 1 at 200 Street and 216 Street interchanges in the Township, which is the route a home mover's transport permit route would use.

blocks.text: Langley Mobile Home Pad Rental Fees: risks and due diligence

items.t: Verify the home, not the land: search the Manufactured Home Registry for the registered owner and the home's record, because the purchase is a chattel transfer registered there, not a land title transfer. The Registry record does not state the pad rent or the park's zoning.

Moving the home out is its own permit: a transport permit comes from the Manufactured Home Registry, a tax certificate for transport is required (with an exception for a move to a different pad in the same park), and the permit expires 30 days after issue.
Check the CSA label: a home may not be sold without its original legible CSA decal, and a lost label requires Technical Safety BC re-certification.

faq.q: How much is pad rent in Langley?
faq.a: A pad rent is set park by park in the written Manufactured Home Site Tenancy Agreement; the figure that matters is the specific park's current rent, obtained from the park and the tenancy agreement before an offer.

faq.q: How much can pad rent go up each year?
faq.a: Up to the yearly limit set by the Residential Tenancy Branch: for 2026, 2.3% plus a proportional amount; for 2027, 2.2% plus the proportional amount. The proportional amount is the change in local government levies plus the change in regulated park utility fees, divided by the number of sites in the park. Increases require 3 full months' notice and can occur only once every 12 months; anything above the limit requires an RTB order.

faq.q: Does the park raise my pad rent when I buy the home?
faq.a: No. On assignment under s. 28 of the MHPTA, the pad rent for the new tenant stays the same and the scheduled date of a subsequent rent increase does not change; the landlord's prior written consent is required (or deemed given) and the landlord cannot charge a fee for consent.

Three verified pad-rental parks, all in Brookswood in the Township: Cedar Creek Estates (3031 200 St), Fernridge Park (20071 24 Ave) and Pineridge (2270 196 St). Pioneer Park in Aldergrove is 55+ but is a co-operative, not a pad-rental park. Other Langley parks — Langley Grove Estates and Aldergrove Mobile Home Park — state no age restrictions in their listings.

faq.q: Can a park refuse me because of age?
faq.a: In a 55+ park, yes on assignment: the MHPTA Regulation recognises a park where every site is reserved for a tenant who has reached 55 and allows the landlord to refuse an assignment where the proposed purchaser does not meet the park's age requirement. That is a park rule under tenancy law — the strata exemptions for younger spouses, caregivers and legacy residents do not automatically apply, so ask the park for its rule in writing.

faq.q: What does pad rent include in a Langley park?
faq.a: Not confirmed as a general statement — inclusions are set park by park in the written site tenancy agreement. Do not budget from a generic "usually includes" list; read the specific agreement for utilities, garbage, water/sewer and amenity charges before writing.

faq.q: What is the monthly cost stack besides pad rent?
faq.a: In structure, not figures: pad rent under the regulated formula, plus home insurance, plus property tax on the home's assessed value excluding the land in a park, plus utilities as the specific park's agreement allocates them. No dollar figure for any element is stated here, because no official source publishes a Langley figure for any of them.

faq.q: What happens if the park is sold or converted to another use?
faq.a: Under MHPTA s. 42: the landlord must first have all necessary permits and approvals, then give 12 months' notice and pay the tenant $20,000 compensation on or before the effective date; the tenant may leave early on 10 days' written notice, may dispute within 15 days, and may in defined circumstances claim additional compensation of the home's assessed value minus the $20,000; if the landlord does not proceed within a reasonable period, a further payment of the greater of $5,000 or 12 months' rent applies.

faq.q: How is Pioneer Park's $510/month different from pad rent?
faq.a: It is a co-op fee, not pad rent — and it is listing-stated, not a published tariff. Listings state the Pioneer Park buyer must be accepted by the co-op, must purchase co-op shares ($9,200 in one listing, refunded upon sale) and pays a monthly co-op fee ($510 in the same listing) rather than pad rent to a landlord. Confirm the current figures with the co-op.

faq.q: Do I pay property tax on a manufactured home in a Langley park?
faq.a: Yes, on the home: the Province states a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value does not include the value of the land where the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.

faq.q: In a Langley park, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad. The exception forms are different products entirely: a fee-simple lot, a bare-land strata lot, or a co-op share (Pioneer Park) — none of which carries MHPTA pad rent.

faq.q: Do I pay property tax on a manufactured home in a Langley park?
faq.a: Yes, on the home: the Province states a manufactured home owner is assessed and taxed like other residential property owners, but the assessed value does not include the value of the land where the home is in a manufactured home park not on reserve land, or on land privately owned by someone other than the home owner.
